newsitem.title: MACAU: Macau activists fight Japanese claim to isles.
newsitem.headline: Macau activists fight Japanese claim to isles.

text.p: An ethnic Chinese group in Macau staged an anti-Japanese protest on Sunday to condemn Tokyo's claims to a group of East China Sea islands and said they planned to sail to the islands to reclaim China's sovereignty.
Donned in black tee-shirts with words "protect the Diaoyu islands", about 100 members of a Chinese sports club marched to the local Xinhua News Agency, China's de facto embassy in the territory.
Waving banners "Japanese dogs get out of the Diaoyu islands" and national flags of the People's Republic of China, they presented a list of 30,000 signatures to a Xinhua official.
A protest leader told reporters an identical list would be hand-delivered to the Japanese consulate in Hong Kong on Monday and spoke of plans to sail to the islets.

"We are planning to hire a ship...to our Chinese Diaoyu islands so that we can erect the Chinese flag there," Chan Kok Keung, president of the Macau Ching Wa Sports and Entertainment Club, told reporters.

The uninhabited rocky outcrops in the East China Sea have kindled fiery passions among Chinese communities in Hong Kong, China, Taiwan and Macau since Japanese right-wing extremists built a lighthouse and planted flags there in July.
Tokyo has claimed sovereign rights to the islands, known by Japan as the Senkakus and by China as the Diaoyus, since 1895.
China has claimed sovereignty over the islands for centuries. Taiwan also lays claim to the territory.
Protests reached new heights last week when Hong Kong activist David Chan drowned after jumping off a protest ship in defiance of a Japanese blockade of the islands.
Chan Kok Keung said 40 members of the club planned to hire a ship to sail to the isles from Xiamen, China's coastal Fujian province, failing which they would begin their sea voyage from Macau.
